newsitem.title: USA: CSFB analyst details Bankers Trust buy rating.
newsitem.headline: CSFB analyst details Bankers Trust buy rating.

text.p: -- Credit Suisse First Boston analyst Brad Ball said he initiated coverage of Bankers Trust New York Corp with a buy rating after the market close on Thursday, ahead of the announcement that the company would tie up with Japanese bank Nippon Credit Bank Ltd.
-- The rating does not reflect the tie up, he said, although he views the announcement favorably.

-- "Bankers Trust is going to get into a relationship that exposes them to credit quality problems in Japan. But they will be in a position to expand in markets around the world, and also in Japan," Ball said.

-- Ball has confidence that management will be able to implement a growth and recovery strategy and said the stock, which has a high dividend yield of 5.1 percent, is selling at a fifteen percent discount to other multinational banks.
-- He said the stock's dramatic sell-off has made it weak against both the bank group and the Standard & Poor's 500. The sell-off is "to a large degree unjustified," he said.
-- Stock has fallen 18 percent from its high a month ago of 96-3/8.

-- He said even a modest improvement in the bank's efficiency ratio, currently 78 or 79 percent, would boost earnings per share. Raising the efficiency ratio is part of the bank's growth and recovery strategy.
-- "Even a five percent improvement would provide strong earnings growth of roughly 10 percent over the next three years. That's very do-able," Ball said.
-- He also said the company is potentially a takeover candidate, although not in the next year or two.
-- "With the Wolfensohn acquisition and now Alex. Brown Inc, they become more attractive as a takeover target by rounding out their glpbal advisery capabilities," he said.
